After signing in you land wherever your personal account says — the branch, network and starting page are all chosen there.

overview.onlineSubtitle: The network link and widget are built in the branch's "Online booking" section — these are just the rules

onlineItems.link: The network link is one booking form for every branch: the client picks a branch first, then a service and time; the booking lands in the chosen branch's journal.

onlineItems.clientPick: The client picks the branch themselves and books straight into it — in the spirit of our "who's free near me right now" catalog.

telephony.notifyBody: Once telephony is connected, each staff member can enable "Incoming calls" under Staff → profile → Notifications — on by default. A call from a known client pops up a card with their last visit and a button to book; from there you can also reschedule or cancel their upcoming visit.
telephony.multiLocationTitle: One connection — the whole network at once
telephony.multiLocationBody: The token and routes are connected once for the whole network: every selected branch gets its own id inside the shared connection, no need to connect telephony separately in each branch.
telephony.vendorBody: When connecting from the marketplace, the vendor receives the location id and network id (plus the list of all branch ids) together with the token from this screen. Access must be activated within an hour of being issued, otherwise the connection expires and has to be redone.
telephony.perLocationBillingBody: After the trial, billing and disconnection are tracked separately per branch: a missed payment turns the integration off only there, and it switches back on within an hour of a refund being reversed — with no effect on the network's other branches.

loyaltyInfo.emptyHint: Your network has no program yet — start with a card type or a certificate
loyaltyInfo.locationsBody: Each card type, certificate, membership and account type has its own branch list. Bonuses on a card marked for every branch can be spent in any of them; if each promotion has its own accrual branch but the card type is open network-wide, bonuses earned across all promotions can be spent anywhere.
loyaltyInfo.sourceTitle: Where the numbers for cumulative promotions come from
loyaltyInfo.sourceBody: "Whole network" counts visits across every branch; "Active branches" counts only the branches marked in "Active in branches" (the default for a new card type); "Loyalty card" follows the card's own branches. The start date cuts off history — visits before it never enter the running total.
loyaltyInfo.crossLocationTitle: Bought in one branch, used in another
loyaltyInfo.crossLocationBody: A certificate or membership can be sold in one branch and redeemed in another regardless of this setting. What is decided separately is where the client is allowed to change its balance and expiry: "Nowhere", "Only in the branch of sale" or "In every branch of the network"; inside the network itself it can always be edited, whatever this setting says.
loyaltyInfo.filtersBody: Certificates, memberships, cards and transactions each carry separate "place of sale" and "place of use" filters — two different branches. There is no "issue card" button in the network list: issuing only happens from the client card or an Excel upload.
loyaltyInfo.accountsTitle: Client accounts: type in the network, operation in the branch
loyaltyInfo.accountsBody: The account type is created in the network and opened only for the branches it is allowed in. Opening, topping up or charging an account only happens in the client's branch; the network shows the full list of accounts and operations, with no top-up button.
loyaltyInfo.onlineSalesTitle: Online sales and revenue by branch
loyaltyInfo.onlineSalesBody: Money from online membership and certificate sales goes to one chosen branch, which gets its own register for it. Splitting revenue across several branches only works with a separate network per branch — everything sold in such a network only applies to its single branch.
loyaltyInfo.saleButtonBody: The shared network widget has no separate switch for the membership/certificate sale button: if a branch's own form points to a network for sales, the button appears only once that branch is selected; to show it for every branch, the network has to be set in each branch's own form.
loyaltyInfo.paymentAccountBody: If a payment provider is already connected in one branch, connecting a second one lets the owner choose: "Use the same account" (one legal entity for every branch) or "Create a new one" (a different entity or a separate network). The same choice applies to the online-sales account.
loyaltyInfo.catalogBody: A membership or certificate created in the network shows up in the branch as a ready-made product — under Goods in its own "Network memberships" group — and can be sold right away from the journal's Sell action.
loyaltyInfo.legacyTitle: The branch's old loyalty vs. the network's
loyaltyInfo.legacyBody: A branch keeps its own "Loyalty program" section — it predates the network one and does less: only automatic discounts by category and client class, plus an SMS when a discount ends. Both run side by side, but new promotions and cards are set up in the network from now on.
loyaltyInfo.notificationsTitle: Network loyalty notifications — network only, by SMS
loyaltyInfo.notificationsBody: Notifications for network cards, promotions and memberships are set up here, not in the branch's "Notifications", and go out naming the network. Client reminders in our own app stay a push, not an SMS.
loyaltyInfo.networkOnlyTitle: Promotions only take network services and products
loyaltyInfo.networkOnlyBody: A branch-only service or product can't be picked for a promotion, certificate or membership until it's made network-wide (via "Migration"). If a promotion only marks a category, it covers every service in it — network and branch alike.
